top_categories.workout_context: When someone attacks on rolling paved loops with five timed climbs, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.

Road-specific control matters at Chasing Cancellara Granfondo Vaduz. Practice on rolling paved loops with five timed climbs: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 60 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Chasing Cancellara Granfondo Vaduz's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
69ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Chasing Cancellara Granfondo Vaduz, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Chasing Cancellara Granfondo Vaduz. Train it until it feels boring.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Chasing Cancellara Granfondo Vaduz. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
60 miles on rolling paved loops with five timed climbs burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on rolling paved loops with five timed climbs can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Varied gradients on rolling paved loops with five timed climbs demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Base fitness for Chasing Cancellara Granfondo Vaduz. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
